questions.problem: Given that $f(x)=2{e}^{x}+4{x}^{2}-3$, find the slope of the tangent at $x=1.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, using the addition and the power rules, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2{e}^{x}+4{x}^{2}-3) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2{e}^{x})+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(4{x}^{2})+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-3) \\  & =2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({e}^{x})+4\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2})+0 \\  & =2{e}^{x}+8x.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent at $x=1$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=1} & ={(2{e}^{x}+8x)\,|}_{x=1} \\  & =2\cdot {e}^{1}+8\cdot 1 \\  & =2e+8.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Given that $f(x)=3\cdot {4}^{x}-2{e}^{x}$, the slope of the tangent at $x=1$ is{{field-1}}.
questions.worked_solution:
Applying the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3\cdot {4}^{x}-2{e}^{x}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3\cdot {4}^{x})-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2{e}^{x}) \\  & =3\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({4}^{x})-2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({e}^{x}) \\  & =3\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)\cdot {4}^{x}-2{e}^{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent at $x=1$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=1} & ={(3\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)\cdot {4}^{x}-2{e}^{x})|}_{x=1} \\  & =3\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)\cdot {4}^{1}-2{e}^{1} \\  & =12\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)-2e.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
